passage: At the community pool, four children were learning to swim in different ways. Francis was afraid of water, so he began in the shallow end, standing and splashing. If he could feel safe there, he told himself, floating would be the next step. Sameer watched an older swimmer's arms and copied the movement on the poolside. Once in the pool, under the coach's eye, he tried it, and the coach corrected the position of his elbow. Neel wanted to impress his friends and jumped into the deep end when the coach was not looking. He panicked and had to be pulled out by the lifeguard, who wrapped a towel around him. The coach sat down with him, and Neel understood that being brave is not the same as being able. Pooja sank every time she tried to float. The coach noticed that she was stiff. She took a slow breath, loosened her arms and let the water hold her up.

qa.q: Where did Francis start his practice?
qa.a: Francis started by standing in the shallow end and splashing.

qa.q: How does Neel's choice differ from Sameer's, and what happened to each?
qa.a: Neel jumped into the deep end to impress friends and had to be pulled out, while Sameer copied a swimmer's arms and had the coach correct his elbow.

qa.q: What was Neel probably feeling when he was pulled out of the water?
qa.a: He was frightened and shaken; the panic in the water showed him he was not ready.

qa.q: What could Neel do next to build his skill safely?
qa.a: He could practise in the shallow end with the coach and move deeper only when the coach says so. 🙂

grounding: Four children learn to swim by starting in the shallows, copying strokes, jumping in the deep end to seem brave, and relaxing the body to float.
